ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What are guide words? (1 mark)
   A. Words that rhyme
   B. The first and last words on a dictionary page
   C. The longest words in the book
   D. The words on the cover

2. Which of these shows how to say a word? (1 mark)
   A. The cover
   B. The page number
   C. The sound guide next to the headword
   D. The index of the atlas

3. What is a surname? (1 mark)
   A. Your family name
   B. Your first name
   C. Your school
   D. Your address

4. Which word has both the sounds /ɔɪ/ and /l/? (1 mark)
   A. boy
   B. toy
   C. oil
   D. road

5. Target sounds: Which word has the sound /ɜː/? (1 mark)
   A. girl
   B. toy
   C. party
   D. five

6. 'Practice makes perfect' teaches us that (1 mark)
   A. practice is a waste of time
   B. we should never try
   C. the more we practise, the better we become
   D. perfect people never practise

7. What do we say when a friend wins a prize? (1 mark)
   A. Excuse me
   B. I beg your pardon
   C. Congratulations
   D. Good night

8. When do we say 'I beg your pardon'? (1 mark)
   A. When we are hungry
   B. When we win
   C. When we did not hear or we need to say sorry
   D. When we say goodbye

9. Which is the best first step before answering a question on a passage? (1 mark)
   A. Close the book
   B. Write the answer immediately
   C. Read the question and find key words
   D. Copy the passage

10. What should you do at a railway crossing? (1 mark)
   A. Play on the track
   B. Run across
   C. Ride faster
   D. Stop, look and listen

11. In which direction does the sun rise? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. West
   C. East
   D. North

12. Choose the sentence with a superlative. (1 mark)
   A. Chege is tall.
   B. Chege is the tallest boy.
   C. Chege is very tall than Ben.
   D. Chege is taller than Ben.

13. Why is it important to plan a composition? (1 mark)
   A. It stops you from writing
   B. It hides your ideas
   C. It keeps the ideas in order
   D. It makes the story longer without ideas

14. What is a password? (1 mark)
   A. A secret word that only you know
   B. A friend's address
   C. A type of email
   D. A public name

15. How long should a Grade 4 pictorial composition be? (1 mark)
   A. about 60 to 80 words
   B. 500 words
   C. 20 words
   D. 5 words

16. Which sentence uses the past progressive correctly? (1 mark)
   A. I walking to school when it started to rain.
   B. I was walk to school when it started to rain.
   C. I was walking to school when it started to rain.
   D. I am walking to school when it started to rain.

17. Which sentence is in the present progressive? (1 mark)
   A. The teacher marked our books.
   B. The teacher had marked our books.
   C. The teacher marks our books.
   D. The teacher is marking our books.

18. Which are pests? (1 mark)
   A. Tall trees
   B. Small animals or insects that damage crops
   C. Sacks for storing maize
   D. Tools for digging

19. What is compost made from, according to Mama Neema? (1 mark)
   A. Cement and sand
   B. Vegetable peelings and dry leaves
   C. Maize flour
   D. Plastic and stones

20. What does it mean to read in phrases? (1 mark)
   A. To read groups of words that go together
   B. To read one letter at a time
   C. To read only the first word of each line
   D. To read backwards

21. Which is the correct negative of 'He works on the farm'? (1 mark)
   A. He doesn't work on the farm.
   B. He doesn't works on the farm.
   C. He don't work on the farm.
   D. He isn't work on the farm.

22. Which sentence has a double negative that should be corrected? (1 mark)
   A. I don't have a pencil.
   B. I don't have no pencil.
   C. I don't have any pencils.
   D. I have no pencil.

23. Which part of a narrative tells who, where and when? (1 mark)
   A. The middle
   B. The end
   C. The beginning
   D. The title

24. Which word begins with a silent h? (1 mark)
   A. house
   B. honest
   C. help
   D. hand

25. Which word begins with the cluster 'sw'? (1 mark)
   A. broom
   B. sweep
   C. green
   D. clean

26. What does 'Prevention is better than cure' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Cure is easy
   B. Medicine is always better
   C. Avoid all doctors
   D. It is better to stop a problem than to solve it later

27. Which syllable is stressed in 'com-POUND'? (1 mark)
   A. Both equally
   B. The first
   C. The second
   D. Neither

28. What is a headline? (1 mark)
   A. A short bold title that tells what a news story is about
   B. A photograph
   C. The writer's name
   D. An advert

29. Which sentence uses the correct preposition for a public vehicle? (1 mark)
   A. He is on the bus.
   B. He is in the bus.
   C. He is at the bus inside.
   D. He is by the bus in.

30. What is the -ing form of 'stop'? (1 mark)
   A. stoping
   B. stopping
   C. stopeing
   D. stoppping

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain the difference between intensive and extensive reading. (3 marks)

32. Write an invitation of three sentences to a wedding or birthday party, using 'invite' and 'decorate'. (3 marks)

33. Why is it important to interpret road signs correctly? (2 marks)

34. Correct these sentences: (a) 'I have money enough to buy bread.' (b) 'She has alot of friends.' (2 marks)

35. Describe how to skim and how to scan a passage. (4 marks)

36. Explain how /v/ and /w/ are made differently. (2 marks)

37. Explain why 'more better' is wrong. Give the correct form. (2 marks)

38. Write two words in which 'gh' is silent and two in which it says /f/. (4 marks)

39. Change to negative statements: (a) She sells eggs. (b) They picked coffee. (4 marks)

40. Correct these sentences: (a) Who did scored the goal? (b) When you will come? (3 marks)

41. Explain what Baraka learnt from his grandmother. (4 marks)

42. Write a diary entry of about 60 words about a day at school. Include the date, feelings and a plan for tomorrow. (5 marks)

43. Write two minimal pairs for /t/ and /d/. (2 marks)

44. Explain what it means to speak with expression. (2 marks)

45. Give two pieces of advice for staying safe online. (3 marks)

46. Write a narrative of about 60 words about a visit to a farm. Include a beginning, a middle, an end and a simile. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — The first and last words on a dictionary page
   They show which words can be found on the page.

2. C — The sound guide next to the headword
   Dictionaries show pronunciation beside the headword.

3. A — Your family name
   The surname is the family name.

4. C — oil
   Oil has /ɔɪ/ followed by /l/.

5. A — girl
   Girl has the long vowel /ɜː/.

6. C — the more we practise, the better we become
   Repeating a skill helps us improve.

7. C — Congratulations
   Congratulations shows we are happy for someone.

8. C — When we did not hear or we need to say sorry
   It asks a person to repeat or says sorry.

9. C — Read the question and find key words
   Key words tell you what to look for in the text.

10. D — Stop, look and listen
   Trains cannot stop quickly.

11. C — East
   The sun rises in the east.

12. B — Chege is the tallest boy.
   The tallest points to the top of three or more.

13. C — It keeps the ideas in order
   A plan shows what comes first, next and last.

14. A — A secret word that only you know
   A password protects your account.

15. A — about 60 to 80 words
   The design asks for about 60 to 80 words.

16. C — I was walking to school when it started to rain.
   Past progressive was + verb-ing, with the simple past for the shorter action.

17. D — The teacher is marking our books.
   Is + verb-ing shows an action happening now.

18. B — Small animals or insects that damage crops
   Pests eat or damage crops.

19. B — Vegetable peelings and dry leaves
   Compost heaps are made of peelings and dry leaves.

20. A — To read groups of words that go together
   Chunking words into phrases makes reading smoother.

21. A — He doesn't work on the farm.
   After doesn't, the verb returns to its base form.

22. B — I don't have no pencil.
   Use only one negative word.

23. C — The beginning
   The beginning introduces characters, setting and time.

24. B — honest
   'Honest' is said 'onest'.

25. B — sweep
   'Sweep' begins with s and w.

26. D — It is better to stop a problem than to solve it later
   Stopping problems early saves effort.

27. C — The second
   The stress falls on 'pound'.

28. A — A short bold title that tells what a news story is about
   The headline gives the subject of a story.

29. A — He is on the bus.
   We say 'on the bus'.

30. B — stopping
   Double the last consonant of a short verb ending in one vowel and one consonant.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Intensive reading is reading a short text closely, often with the class, to understand it fully. Extensive reading is choosing materials and reading a lot on your own for pleasure and learning.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for the difference in choice or amount.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: I invite you to my sister's wedding on Saturday. We will decorate the hall with flowers. Please come at ten o'clock.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: Signs warn us of danger and tell us what to do, so misunderstanding one could cause an accident.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for what signs do and 1 mark for the danger of misunderstanding.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) I have enough money to buy bread. (b) She has a lot of friends.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: To skim, look at the title, pictures and the first sentence of each paragraph to get the main idea. To scan, look quickly for key words to find a particular fact.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for skimming and 2 marks for scanning.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: For /v/ the upper teeth touch the lower lip and the voice buzzes; for /w/ the lips are rounded and do not touch the teeth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Better is already the comparative form, so we do not add more. The correct form is better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the reason and 1 mark for the correct form.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Silent: night, light, high, daughter (any two). /f/: laugh, cough, enough, rough (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: (a) She doesn't sell eggs. (b) They didn't pick coffee.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks each: 1 for the correct helping verb, 1 for the base form of the main verb.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) Who scored the goal? (b) When will you come?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correction and 1 for question marks and capitals.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: He learnt that ugali and tea are not enough. A balanced diet with energy foods, body-building foods, fruit and vegetables and clean water keeps a person strong and healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct points.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: An entry in the first person with a date, events in order, feelings, a plan and a sign-off.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the date, 1 for events in order, 1 for feelings, 1 for a plan, 1 for correct tense and punctuation.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: ten, den and tin, din.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: It means using the voice to show meaning and feeling by changing loudness, stress and pitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using the voice and 1 for showing feeling or meaning.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not give your name, school or address to strangers. Show worrying messages to a trusted adult. Ask a parent or teacher before opening a new page.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct piece of advice, up to 3.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: A story of about 60 words in the past tense with clear parts and a simile.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the beginning, 1 for events in order, 1 for the end, 1 for a simile, 1 for correct tense and punctuation.
